p.src: Now, after leaving Xichun in a fit of anger, Lady You was about to go to Lady Wang's quarters. The old serving-women accompanying her quietly advised, “Madam, you had better not go to the main apartments just yet. Several people from the Zhen family have just arrived, bringing some things with them, and we do not know what secret business is afoot. It might be awkward if you went there now.” Lady You replied, “Yesterday I heard your master say that the court gazette reported the Zhen family guilty of an offence. Their property is now being confiscated, and they have been summoned to the capital to stand trial. Why, then, have more of their people come here?” “That is precisely what puzzles us,” said the old woman. “Several women arrived just now, looking utterly distraught and flustered. I dare say they have some business they wish to conceal.” Hearing this, Lady You went no farther but returned instead to Li Wan's rooms. The imperial physician had only just finished taking her pulse and left. Li Wan had lately begun to feel somewhat more alert. Wrapped in her quilt and propped against her pillows, she sat upon the bed wishing that one or two people might come and chat with her. But when Lady You entered, she lacked her customary warmth and friendliness and merely sat there in a daze. Li Wan therefore asked, “You have been here half the day. Did you have anything to eat in any of the other rooms? I fear you must be hungry.” She told Suyun to see what fresh pastries there were and bring a selection. Lady You hurriedly stopped her. “There is no need, truly. You have been ill all this while; how could there be anything fresh here? Besides, I am not hungry.” Li Wan said, “Yesterday her aunt's family sent over some excellent roasted-flour tea. Let them mix you a bowl of that.” With that, she ordered a servant to prepare the tea. Lady You remained lost in thought and said nothing. The maids and married serving-women who had accompanied her asked, “Madam, you have not washed your face since midday. Shall we take this opportunity to freshen you up?” Lady You nodded. Li Wan at once told Suyun to fetch her dressing case. As Suyun brought it over, she also produced her own rouge and powder, saying with a smile, “This is the one thing our mistress does not have. If you do not mind its being unclean, Madam, this is mine; perhaps you could use a little.” Li Wan said, “Though I have none, you ought to have fetched some from the young ladies. How could you openly bring out your own? It is fortunate that it is she; would anyone else not take offence?” Lady You laughed. “What does that matter? Whenever I have come here before, whose things have I not used? Why should I suddenly find them unclean today?” As she spoke, she sat cross-legged on the edge of the kang. Yindie hurried forward to remove her bracelets and rings, then spread a large towel over her lower body to protect her clothes completely. The young maid Chaodou'er carried a large basin of warm water over to Lady You and merely stood bent at the waist, holding it before her. Li Wan said, “What sort of manners are those?” Yindie laughed. “When we say they have no adaptability, we mean that if you tell them ‘a gourd,’ a gourd ladle is all they can think of.

But you grow presumptuous and act just as casually whether at home or away, even in front of relatives.” Lady You said, “Leave her be. p.src: Before she had finished speaking, a servant came to announce, “Miss Bao has arrived.” Just as they hurriedly called for her to be shown in, Baochai had already entered. Lady You hastily dried her face, rose, and offered her a seat. Then she asked, “What brings you here alone so suddenly? Why are none of the other girls with you?” Baochai replied, “As it happens, I have not seen them either. Our mistress is unwell today, and the two women in our household are both still bedridden with the seasonal illness. There is no one else dependable, so today I must go out and stay with the old lady to keep her company tonight. I ought to report it to the Old Lady and Lady Wang, but I thought it was no great matter and need not be mentioned for now. I shall come back in any case once she is better, so I came merely to tell you, Sister-in-law.” On hearing this, Li Wan merely looked at Lady You and smiled. Lady You likewise merely looked at Li Wan and smiled. Presently Lady You finished washing, and they all had bowls of roasted-flour tea. Li Wan said with a smile, “In that case, let us first send someone to inquire after your aunt and ask what her illness is. I am ill myself and cannot visit her in person. Dear sister, you may go without concern. I shall send someone to your place to look after your rooms. But you must come back after a day or two, or people will blame me.” Baochai laughed. “Why should anyone blame you? This is only ordinary human feeling; it is not as though you had taken a bribe to let a thief escape. If you ask me, there is no need to send more people over there. Simply invite Yun to come here and stay with you for a day or two. Would that not save trouble?” Lady You asked, “By the way, where has our young Cousin Shi gone?” Baochai replied, “I have just sent them to look for her at your Cousin Tan's. I told them to bring her here, so that I could explain everything to her myself.”

p.src: As they were speaking, someone duly announced, “Miss Yun and the Third Young Lady have arrived.” After everyone had exchanged courtesies and taken their seats, Baochai mentioned that she intended to leave. Tanchun said, “That is an excellent idea. You may return when your aunt has recovered, but even if you do not come back after she recovers, that will be quite all right.” Lady You laughed. “What a strange thing to say! Why are you driving your relatives away?” Tanchun gave a cold laugh. “Precisely! Rather than wait for someone else to drive her away, I would sooner do it first. Relatives can remain on good terms without having to live together to the bitter end. We, on the other hand, are flesh and blood of one family, yet every one of us is like a pair of fighting cocks, each longing to devour the other!” Lady You hurriedly laughed. “What ill luck brought me here today, just when every one of you sisters is in such a temper?” “Who told you to come warming yourself at the hot stove?” said Tanchun. Then she asked, “Who has offended you now?” Reflecting further, she said, “The Fourth Young Lady would hardly pick a quarrel with you. Who could it be?” Lady You merely gave an evasive reply. Knowing that Lady You feared trouble and would say no more, Tanchun laughed. “Do not pretend to be so meek. No one will be beheaded unless the Imperial Court condemns them, so you need not be afraid of everything. To tell you the truth, yesterday I struck that old woman, Wang Shanbao’s wife, and I am still bearing the blame for it. At worst she will gossip about me behind my back. Surely she cannot give me a beating!” Baochai quickly asked why she had struck the woman, and Tanchun related in full how the search had been conducted the previous night and how she had hit her. Since Tanchun had already spoken openly, Lady You also told them what had just happened with Xichun. “That is her peculiar temperament,” said Tanchun. “She is far too aloof and unbending; none of us can surpass her in pride.” She went on to tell them, “There was no sign of anything early this morning, but then I heard that Spitfire Feng was ill again. So I sent my nurse out to discover what had become of Wang Shanbao’s wife. She returned and told me that Wang Shanbao’s wife had received a beating and that the Elder Lady was angry with her for meddling.” Lady You and Li Wan said, “That is only right.” Tanchun sneered. “Anyone can put on such a show to cover things up. Let us wait and see.” Lady You and Li Wan both remained silent and made no reply. Presently, judging that dinner would soon be served in the front apartments, Xiangyun and Baochai returned to their rooms to arrange their clothes. There is no need to relate this further. Lady You and the others then took leave of Li Wan and went to Grandmother Jia’s quarters. Grandmother Jia was reclining on a couch while Lady Wang explained why the Zhen family had been found guilty, how their property had now been confiscated, and how they had been sent back to the capital to face punishment. The news was distressing Grandmother Jia when, fortunately, she saw the ladies arrive. She asked, “Where have you come from? Do you know how Sister Feng and her sister-in-law are today?” Lady You and the others hurriedly replied, “They are both somewhat better today.”

p.src: Grandmother Jia nodded and sighed. “Let us not concern ourselves with other people’s affairs. The proper business is to discuss how we shall admire the moon on the fifteenth of the eighth month.” Lady Wang smiled. “Everything has already been prepared. We do not know which place the Old Lady would prefer, though the garden is rather exposed and the wind is cold at night.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “What harm is there in wearing a few more layers? That is precisely the place for admiring the moon; how could we possibly not go?” While they were speaking, married servants and maids had already carried in the dining table, and Lady Wang, Lady You, and the others hurried forward to lay the chopsticks and serve the rice. When Grandmother Jia saw that her own several dishes had all been laid out and that several more dishes had arrived in two large covered trays, she knew that these were the customary extra offerings of filial respect from the various households. Grandmother Jia asked, “What are they all? I have told you several times already that these extras may now be dispensed with, but still you will not listen. Things are no longer as prosperous and abundant as they once were.” Yuanyang hurriedly said, “I have told them several times, but they will not listen, so there is nothing to be done.” Lady Wang smiled. “They are only ordinary household dishes. As I am observing a fast today, I had nothing else to offer. The Old Lady is not very fond of the gluten or bean curd dishes, so I selected only one dish of finely minced pickles dressed with pepper oil.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “That is just the thing. I was craving it.” Hearing this, Yuanyang moved the dish closer to her. Baoqin invited each of the others to eat before returning to her seat. Grandmother Jia then told Tanchun to join her at the meal. After Tanchun too had invited everyone in turn, she sat down opposite Baoqin. Daishu hurried away to fetch a bowl. Pointing to the other dishes, Yuanyang said, “I cannot tell what these two are. They were sent by the Elder Master. This bowl contains bamboo shoots with chicken marrow, sent up by the Master from the outer quarters.” As she spoke, she placed only the bowl of bamboo shoots on the table. Grandmother Jia tasted a morsel or two, then ordered, “Have those other two dishes sent back and say that I ate some. There is no need to send them every day in future. If I wish to eat them, I shall ask for them myself.” The married servants assented and carried the dishes back. There is no need to relate this further. Grandmother Jia then asked, “Is there any rice gruel? I think I shall have a little.” Lady You promptly presented a bowl, saying that it was red-rice gruel. Grandmother Jia took it and ate half a bowl, then ordered, “Send this gruel to Feng.” Pointing again, she said, “Send this bowl of bamboo shoots and this plate of wind-cured civet to Daiyu and Baoyu, and give that bowl of meat to young Lan.” Then she said to Lady You, “I have finished. You may come and eat now.” Lady You assented. After Grandmother Jia had rinsed her mouth and washed her hands, she descended from the couch and walked about with Lady Wang, chatting as she digested her meal. Lady You asked permission to sit down. Tanchun and Baoqin also rose and said with a laugh, “Pray excuse us for leaving you; pray excuse us.”

p.src: Lady You laughed. “I am not used to dining alone at such a large table.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Yuanyang and Hupo can take the opportunity to eat with you and keep you company.” Lady You laughed. “Good, good, excellent! I was just about to suggest it.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “There is nothing more delightful than watching a great many people eat.” Then, pointing at Yindie, she said, “This girl may join you too. Come and eat with your mistress. Once you have left me, you may observe the rules again.” Lady You said, “Come over quickly. There is no need to stand on ceremony.” Grandmother Jia stood with her hands clasped behind her back, watching them with amusement. Seeing that the servant who had come to replenish the rice was holding a bowl of the coarser rice served to the household staff, while Lady You was still eating polished white rice, Grandmother Jia asked, “Have you lost your wits? Why have you brought that rice for your mistress?” The servant replied, “Your Ladyship's rice has all been eaten. As one more young lady joined us today, we ran a little short.” Yuanyang said, “Nowadays everything is measured to the last grain, like making a hat to fit the exact size of the head. There cannot be the least bit to spare.” Madam Wang hastily explained, “For the past year or two, droughts and floods have been so unpredictable that the estates have been unable to deliver their full quotas of rice. These finer varieties are harder still to obtain, so we issue only as much as will actually be eaten, for fear that if we suddenly run short, whatever we buy elsewhere will not suit our taste.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “This is truly a case of ‘even the cleverest housewife cannot make porridge without rice.’” Everyone burst out laughing. Yuanyang said, “In that case, you could simply fetch the Third Young Lady's rice and add some from that. How can you be so witless?” Lady You laughed. “This is enough for me. There is no need to fetch any more.” Yuanyang said, “It may be enough for you, but am I not to eat?” Only then did the married servants waiting below hurry off to fetch it. Presently Madam Wang also went to dine, while Lady You remained with Grandmother Jia, chatting and amusing her. When the first night watch began, Grandmother Jia said, “It is dark now. You had better go back.” Only then did Lady You take her leave and go out. She reached the main gate and entered her carriage, while Yindie sat on its edge. The married servants lowered the curtain, then took the young maids ahead of the carriage and went straight to wait at the main gate of the other residence. The gates of the two mansions were less than an arrow's flight apart. Since people came and went between them every day without needing a full ceremonial escort—and made the return journey even more often after dark—the old nursemaids and young maids covered the distance in only a few steps. The gatekeepers of both mansions had gone to the eastern and western ends of the street and had already stopped all passersby. No draught animal was needed for Lady You's great carriage. Seven or eight young male servants merely took hold of its rings and wheels and gently pushed and pulled it up onto the stone landing before the gate. The young servants then withdrew beyond the stone lions. The nursemaids raised the curtain, Yindie alighted first, and then they helped Lady You down.

p.src: Seven or eight lanterns, large and small, illuminated everything with perfect clarity. Seeing four or five large carriages standing beside the stone lions on either side, Lady You knew that they belonged to men who had come to gamble. She said to Yindie and the others, “Look at this! There are so many who came by carriage; who knows how many more came on horseback? Naturally, their horses are tethered in the enclosure, where we cannot see them. p.src: In the inner room, a more genteel group was playing dominoes at Heaven and Nine. The attendants here were all boys under fifteen; no grown man was admitted. That was why Lady You had been able to steal up outside the window and peer in. Among them were two handsome youths of sixteen or seventeen kept to serve wine, both made up and dressed with exquisite beauty. Today Xue Pan had lost again on the first throw and was in a foul temper. Fortunately, when the second throw was completed and the accounts reckoned, the tables had turned and he had actually won, so his spirits rose at once. Jia Zhen said, “Let us stop for now and eat before we begin again.” He then asked how the other two groups were faring. The Heaven and Nine players in the inner room had also settled their accounts and were waiting to eat. But the gongfan game was not yet settled, and its players refused to eat for the moment. Since neither group could be hurried, a great table was laid first for the others, with Jia Zhen keeping them company; Jia Rong was instructed to stay behind and attend the remaining group later. Xue Pan was in high spirits. He put an arm around one of the handsome youths as he drank and ordered wine to be taken over to Uncle Xing the Fool. Uncle Fool had been losing and was out of sorts. After two bowls he became somewhat drunk and, annoyed that the two youths attended only to the winners and ignored the losers, cursed them: “You little catamites always know which way the current runs and fawn on those upstream. We are together every day, and whose favors have you not enjoyed? Yet merely because I have lost a few taels of silver just now, you begin sorting us into ranks. Do you imagine you will never again have occasion to ask a favor of us?” Seeing that the wine was speaking through him, the others hastily said, “Quite right, quite right. Their manners truly are deplorable.” They then shouted at the youths, “Hurry and offer him wine in apology!” The two youths were well rehearsed in such routines. They promptly knelt and offered wine, saying, “People in our profession are taught by our masters to make no distinction between near and distant or favored and neglected, but simply to honor and attend anyone who happens to possess money and influence, regarding him as a living Buddha or immortal. The moment he loses his wealth and power, we are forbidden even to notice him. Besides, we are young and occupy this lowly station. We beg Your Lordship to show us some indulgence and let the matter pass.” As they spoke, they held up the wine and sank to their knees before him. Although Uncle Xing’s heart had softened, he still feigned anger and ignored them. The others urged him again: “The boys have spoken honestly. You have always known how to cherish youth and beauty, Uncle; why behave so differently today? If you will not drink their wine, how can the two of them rise?” Uncle Xing could hold out no longer and said, “Were it not for all of you speaking on their behalf, I would never pay them any heed again.” With that, he took the bowl and drained it in one breath. Another bowl was poured for him. The wine now stirred old memories in Uncle Xing, and in his drunkenness he began to reveal his true feelings. Slapping the table, he sighed to Jia Zhen, “No wonder they value money as their very lives. How many people born into great families of hereditary officials will, at the mere mention of ‘money and power,’ refuse to acknowledge even their own flesh and blood!”

p.src: As promised, Jia Zhen had a whole pig boiled and an entire sheep roasted; the other table dishes, fruits, and delicacies were too numerous to count. In the Conglü Hall of Huifang Garden, peacock screens were unfolded and lotus-patterned cushions laid out as he gathered his wife and concubines about him. They dined first and drank afterward, giving themselves up to merriment as they admired the moon. Toward the first watch, the breeze was fresh and the moon brilliant, bathing everything above and below in silver. When Jia Zhen proposed a drinking game, Madam You called Peifeng and three other girls to join the feast. They sat in a row at the lower end, played finger-guessing games, and drank for a while. A few cups made Jia Zhen still more exuberant. He ordered a purple-bamboo flute brought in, had Peifeng play it and Wenhua sing; her voice was so pure and tender that it fairly ravished the soul. When the song ended, they resumed their drinking games. By the time the third watch drew near, Jia Zhen was eight-tenths drunk. Just as everyone was putting on warmer clothes, drinking tea, and changing cups to drink afresh, they suddenly heard someone heave a long sigh beneath the wall nearby. They had all heard it distinctly and were seized with alarm and dread. Jia Zhen hastily thundered, “Who is there?” He called several times, but no one answered. Madam You said, “Perhaps it was someone from our household outside the wall.” “Nonsense,” said Jia Zhen. There are no servants’ quarters anywhere around this wall, and that side stands directly against the ancestral hall. How could anyone be there?” Before he had finished, they heard a gust of wind sweep over the wall. Dimly, they seemed to hear the lattice doors in the ancestral hall opening and closing. An eerie chill filled the air, colder than before; the moonlight turned wan and was no longer so bright. Everyone felt their hair stand on end. Jia Zhen sobered by half. Though he maintained his composure better than the others, he too was deeply apprehensive and quite lost his taste for the festivities. After forcing himself to remain seated a little longer, he returned to his room to rest. Early the next morning, the fifteenth, he led the younger men of the family to open the ancestral hall and perform the rites observed on the new and full moons. A careful inspection showed everything inside to be just as before, with no trace of anything strange. Jia Zhen concluded that drink had made him imagine strange things and said nothing of the matter. When the rites were over, they closed the doors again, and he watched them securely locked. Jia Zhen and his wife did not come over to the Rong mansion until after the evening meal. They found Jia She and Jia Zheng in Grandmother Jia’s room, chatting idly and amusing her. Jia Lian, Baoyu, Jia Huan, and Jia Lan were all standing in attendance below. When Jia Zhen arrived, he exchanged greetings with them all in turn. After a few words, Grandmother Jia told him to sit. Only then did Jia Zhen ask permission to take a seat on a small stool by the door, where he sat sideways with respectful reserve. Grandmother Jia asked with a smile, “How has your cousin Bao’s archery been these past two days?” Jia Zhen hastily rose and replied with a smile, “He has improved greatly. Not only is his form better, but he can now draw a bow one grade stronger.” “That is quite enough,” said Grandmother Jia. “He must not strain after strength and injure himself.”

p.src: The garden’s main gates now stood wide open, with great horn-paneled lanterns hanging from them. Madam Xing and the other ladies had long been waiting inside. Bright moonlight and brilliant lanterns, the warmth of the company and curling incense smoke—all shimmered together in a radiant haze beyond description. Prayer mats and brocade cushions had been spread on the ground. Grandmother Jia washed her hands, offered incense, and bowed; then everyone else performed their bows in turn. Grandmother Jia then said, “The best place to admire the moon is on the hill.” She therefore ordered that they move to the great hall on the ridge. At this, the servants hurried there to make the arrangements. Meanwhile, Grandmother Jia remained in Jiayin Hall, drinking tea, resting briefly, and chatting. Presently someone came to report, “Everything is ready.” Only then did Grandmother Jia, supported by her attendants, begin climbing the hill. Madam Wang and the others said, “The moss on the stones may be slippery. It would be better to go up in a bamboo chair.” Grandmother Jia replied, “It is swept every day, and the path is broad, level, and perfectly safe. Why should I not stretch my limbs a little?” Thus Jia She, Jia Zheng, and the others led the way; two old women carried a pair of horn-paneled hand lanterns, Yuanyang, Hupo, and Madam You supported Grandmother Jia closely, while Madam Xing and the rest followed around her. Tables and chairs had been arranged on the terrace before the hall, and a large folding screen divided the space into two sections. All the tables and chairs were round, deliberately chosen to symbolize family reunion. Grandmother Jia took the central seat at the head. On her left sat Jia She, Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, and Jia Rong in descending order; on her right sat Jia Zheng, Baoyu, Jia Huan, and Jia Lan, all gathered in a circle. I would invite a few more, but they all have parents and must celebrate the occasion at home, so it would not do for them to come. Let us ask the girls to come and sit over there.” Accordingly, a servant was sent behind the screen to Madam Xing’s table to invite Yingchun, Tanchun, and Xichun to join them. Jia Lian, Baoyu, and the others all rose from their seats, allowing the sisters to sit first before taking their own places in order below them. Grandmother Jia then ordered someone to break off a spray of osmanthus and instructed one of the young married women to beat a drum behind the screen while the flower was passed around. p.src: The young ladies and gentlemen secretly tugged or pinched one another, all smiling as they waited to hear what sort of joke it would be. Seeing Grandmother Jia so delighted, Jia Zheng had no choice but to humor her. Just as he was about to begin, Grandmother Jia added with a laugh, “If your joke fails to make us laugh, you must still pay a forfeit.” Jia Zheng laughed. “I know only one. If it fails to amuse you, I shall simply have to accept the forfeit.” Then he began with a smile: “There was once a man who feared his wife more than anyone else in his family.” He had uttered only this one sentence when everyone burst out laughing. They laughed because they had never before heard Jia Zheng tell a joke. Grandmother Jia laughed. “This is sure to be a good one.” Jia Zheng replied with a smile, “If it is, please drink an extra cup, Old Lady.” “Naturally,” Grandmother Jia said, laughing. Jia Zheng continued: “This henpecked husband never dared take a single step farther than he was permitted. But one year, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, he went into the street to buy something and happened to meet several friends, who dragged him home with them and insisted that he drink. He unexpectedly became drunk and fell asleep at his friend’s house. He did not wake until the next day, and by then regret was useless, so he could only go home and beg forgiveness. His wife was washing her feet. She said, ‘Since that is what happened, lick my feet for me and I shall forgive you.’ The man had no choice but to lick them, but the taste made him nauseous and he nearly vomited. His wife flew into a rage and raised her hand to strike him. ‘How dare you treat me with such contempt!’ she cried. Terrified, the husband hurriedly knelt and pleaded, ‘It is certainly not because my lady’s feet are dirty. It is only that I drank too much yellow wine last night and ate several pieces of mooncake filling, so my stomach is rather sour today.’” At this, Grandmother Jia and everyone else burst out laughing. Jia Zheng quickly poured a cup and presented it to Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia laughed. “In that case, have someone bring strong spirits at once, so that none of you will have to suffer.” Everyone laughed again. The drum sounded again, and the flower was passed on from Jia Zheng. By chance, the drumming stopped just as it reached Baoyu. With Jia Zheng present, Baoyu was already nervous and ill at ease; now the flower happened to be in his hand. He thought, “If my joke fails to raise a laugh, they will say I have no wit and cannot even tell a joke, let alone do anything else. That will be held against me. But if I tell it well, they will say I cannot apply myself to serious matters and am skilled only at glib and frivolous chatter. That will be an even greater fault. It would be better not to tell one at all.” He therefore rose and excused himself. “I cannot tell jokes. Please set me some other task instead.” Jia Zheng said, “In that case, I shall give you the word ‘autumn.’ Compose a poem on the scene before us. If it is good, I shall reward you; if not, you had better take care tomorrow.” Grandmother Jia hurriedly protested, “We were enjoying the drinking game perfectly well. Why make him compose a poem now?” “He is capable of it,” said Jia Zheng. Hearing this, Grandmother Jia said, “If so, let him compose it.”

p.src: Unexpectedly, this time the flower fell into Jia Huan's hands. Jia Huan had lately made some progress in his studies, but he shared Baoyu's distaste for applying himself to proper pursuits; he therefore often enjoyed reading poetry, with a particular fondness for strange and fantastical verses about immortals and ghosts. Seeing Baoyu rewarded for his poem, he was itching to display his own skill, though in Jia Zheng's presence he dared not act rashly. Now that the flower had providentially come into his hands, however, he called for paper and brush and dashed off a quatrain for Jia Zheng. After reading it, Jia Zheng too found it unusually striking, but its language still betrayed an aversion to study, so he said displeasedly, “This certainly proves that you are brothers. Everything you say smacks of heterodoxy; in future neither of you will submit to rules or standards, and you will both turn into worthless degenerates. The ancients had their ‘two worthy brothers’; fittingly enough, you two may also be called a pair of ‘difficult brothers.’ Only in your case, the word ‘difficult’ should be understood to mean ‘difficult to discipline.’ The elder openly fancies himself Wen Feiqing, and now the younger imagines himself Cao Tang reborn.” His words made Jia She and the others laugh. Jia She then asked for the poem and read it through. Praising it repeatedly, he said, “In my opinion, this poem has real spirit and backbone. Families like ours are not to be compared with those impoverished scholars who must study by the light reflected from snow or by a firefly's glow until one day they pluck the cassia in the Moon Palace and can at last hold their heads high. The sons of our family should certainly read a few books, but only so that they understand a little more than other people; whenever they are old enough to hold office, an appointment will assuredly be theirs. Why waste so much effort on it, only to turn them into pedants? That is why I like his poem: it does not disgrace the bearing of our marquis's house.” He then turned and ordered a servant to fetch a great many of his own curios and present them to Jia Huan as a reward. Patting Jia Huan on the head, he added with a smile, “Keep writing like this from now on—that is the tone befitting our family. In the future, this hereditary position is certain to fall to you.” Hearing this, Jia Zheng hastily protested, “He merely scribbled some nonsense; how can you already be talking about what will happen in the future?”
